subject: health
title: Food Groups
about: Sorting everyday foods into the five food groups (fruits, vegetables, grains, protein, dairy), what fills each half of the plate, water or milk with meals, a rainbow of colors, and why breakfast matters. NC 1.NPA.1.2 (a variety of foods and why to eat them) and 1.NPA.1.1 (reasons to drink water); builds on Healthy Foods and is all about sorting.
tip: At the grocery store, hand him one food at a time and let him call out its group before it goes in the cart.

cards.q: Which food group is corn in?
cards.note: Corn, potatoes and peas are starchy vegetables.

cards.q: Oatmeal is made from oats. Where does it belong?
cards.note: Oats, wheat, rice and corn flour are all grains.

cards.q: You drink a glass of milk at lunch. What group did you just eat from?
cards.note: Dairy foods give your bones calcium.

cards.q: Which food group is peanut butter in?
cards.note: Nuts, seeds, eggs, fish and meat are all protein foods.

cards.q: Where do grapes and watermelon belong?
cards.note: Fruits are sweet because they have natural sugar.
Spinach, lettuce and kale are leafy green vegetables.
Tortillas are made from corn or wheat flour.
Pears grow on trees, like apples.

cards.q: Turkey goes in the same group as chicken. What group is that?
cards.note: Turkey, chicken, beef and fish are protein foods.

cards.q: You pick a cup of yogurt. Which group did you pick from?
cards.note: Yogurt is made from milk, so it is dairy.

cards.q: Sort a sweet potato. It goes with the...?
cards.note: The sweet potato is North Carolina's state vegetable.

cards.q: Popcorn. Which group does it go in?
cards.note: Popcorn is a whole grain. Plain popcorn is a healthy snack.

cards.q: Fruits and vegetables fill half your plate. What fills the other half?
cards.note: Add a cup of milk or yogurt on the side and you have all five groups.

cards.q: Which drink goes best with your meal?
cards.note: Sugary drinks have lots of sugar and not much your body needs.

cards.q: Which breakfast gives you energy for school?
cards.note: Grains plus a fruit is a great start.
Breakfast means break the fast. Your body has not eaten all night.

cards.q: Eating a rainbow means eating fruits and veggies of many...?
cards.note: Red, orange, green, purple. Each color helps your body a different way.

cards.q: A sandwich has bread, turkey, cheese and lettuce. How many food groups is that?
cards.note: Bread is grains, turkey is protein, cheese is dairy, lettuce is vegetables.
